verses.1: And a prophet prophesied, whose name was Qarub of Remath of Moab, to Syria.
verses.2: And he rent the ground and entered up to his neck, and wept with bitter weeping, and repented of the sin he had committed before God.
verses.3: And thus God said to the prophet: Go to the land of Judah, enter into the land of Remath, to Meqabis, the ruler of Moab, and say to them: Thus says the Lord: Was it not you who made this, that it should not be devoured by the strength of my power? And by my wrath I destroyed the holy city. But I, the Lord, am your protector; by my will I sent you, that you might destroy my city.
verses.4: For from my youth there was in me all deceit, and fornication, and corruption.
verses.5: And I also preserved it and delivered it into your hand; and it was not on your account that you stiffened your neck and said, 'I conquered the city by the strength of my hand.' And now, because of your children whom you begot, they transgressed against God because of your sin.
verses.6: And now repent with all your heart, and be sealed, and do not be doubtful; for those who doubt are not sealed for repentance.
verses.7: But blessed are those who repent with all their heart and do not turn back to filth and sin; in all that they repent of, it is on account of their evil.
verses.8: And they shall be sealed with weeping, and with tears, and with much supplication, and with worship before God who created them; for he says to the penitent: You, after your error and your repentance, are mine.
verses.9: And to the penitent one he says: After your error, when you returned to him in repentance, because of your trembling and your fear you transgressed for your sin. For I, the Lord, am your helper, who requite the sin of the father upon the children to the third and fourth generation; but to those who love me and keep my commandments I show mercy with them for a thousand generations.
verses.10: And now, because of these your children whom you begot, I will keep my covenant with you, and I will add the repentance which I made on account of your evil deeds, says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, who is clothed with all things.
verses.11: And at that time he went out from the meal and bowed down to the prophet, saying thus and thus: May the Lord not forget me, that I should not be separated from you; but remember me according to your will. For I provoked the Lord, and I did not walk in his commandment like my fathers; for we have no law, and to you belongs the wonder, that we should worship idols as our fathers taught us.
verses.12: But I did not listen to the voice of the prophets of the Lord until now; for I am a sinner who walked in my sin, and in the pride of my heart, and in the stiffness of my neck; I provoked the commandment of the Lord, and I did not walk in his commandment, nor in his covenant which he commanded me.
verses.13: And the prophet answered and said to him: I know that now your repentance is confirmed; for there is none before you who trusts in his sins from among your kindred.
verses.14: And from now on, forsake the worship of idols, and turn to the knowledge of God, that your repentance may be in truth. And he bowed down beneath the feet of the prophet; and the prophet arose and commanded him everything that pertains to good works.
verses.15: And he did as the Lord commanded him, and he returned into his house.
verses.16: And this Meqabis also examined himself, and removed from his house every idol, and the idols, and the images, and the objects of worship, and the idols.
verses.17: And the children of Zion whom he had brought from Jerusalem, he taught them morning and evening all the commandment of God, and his law and his ordinances, as their fathers used to do.
verses.18: And he appointed from among the children of Zion, from the wise men, in his house.
verses.19: And again from the young men, from among their wise men, he appointed overseers in their dwellings, who should instruct the young children, their pupils, that they might teach them the way of God, as the children of Israel kept the law and its ordinances, and its covenant, and judgment, and all their sacred things which the Moabites had profaned; he heard it from the children of Zion.
verses.20: And he removed their sacred things, and all their idols, and all their images, and all their altars, and their sacrifices, from their glorious ones, from the hide of his flock, and from the skin of the lamb which he sacrificed to his gods, morning and evening.
verses.21: And he sacrificed to them and worshipped them with every work of incense and of the hour, and he asked them and trusted in them, and did their will in everything that he told those demons, his gods.
verses.22: And he did not depart from their words in all that he told them, for it seemed to him that in everything he was saved.
verses.23: But this Meqabis forsook their way.
verses.24: And when the king heard the word which the prophet spoke to him, he turned his way to repentance, and all his house turned their ways from the children of Israel. In those days, for the children of Israel at one time provoked him, and at times he punished them, they cried out and prayed to God.
verses.25: And when they saw that they were defeated under their hands by the people who oppressed them, and they cried out before him, then he had mercy on them, remembering the covenant of their fathers, when they prayed to him for the sake of Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, their fathers.
verses.26: And when he saved them, they forgot him who saved them, and they returned to the worship of idols.
verses.27: And then he sent against them peoples who oppressed them; and when they oppressed them and afflicted them, they prayed to God, and at that time he had mercy on them and spared them, because he loved them, for they were the work of his hands.
verses.28: And again, when he strengthened them, they returned to provoke him with the worship of idols that surrounded them, and the work of their hands was evil.
verses.29: And he also raised up against them the peoples of Elam, and Moab, and Midian, and Syria, and Egypt; and they wept and prayed when their enemies provoked them, and afflicted them, and enslaved them, and oppressed them; and he raised up for them judges, that the judges might save them.
